title: Impacts of Vulnerabilities in Artisanal Marine Fisheries on Fishing Activities Along the Togolese Coast
content: In Togo, artisanal fishing serves as a source of employment and income while contributing to meeting the population's food needs. In recent decades, however, the sector has faced numerous vulnerabilities stemming from various risks that limit its significant contribution to food security. This article analyzes the impact of these vulnerabilities on artisanal marine fishing within coastal fishing communities in Togo. The methodological approach relies on both secondary and field data, collected via questionnaires and interview guides administered to stakeholders in the artisanal marine fishing value chain. Statistical tools, such as the Chi-square test and Cramer’s V, were used to establish interdependencies between the various analytical variables. The study reveals that artisanal marine fisheries face diverse vulnerabilities—specifically environmental, economic, socio-cultural, and legal-institutional. These factors undermine fishing activities and, by extension, the food security of fishing communities. Economic vulnerabilities are the most acutely felt, affecting 94% of surveyed stakeholders, followed by socio-cultural vulnerabilities (82%) and environmental vulnerabilities (78%). Sustainable fishery management and the promotion of aquaculture offer potential ways to mitigate the impact of these vulnerabilities on artisanal marine fishing activities and food security.
